stories.h: Seattle mayor allows targeted police camera expansion
stories.s: Mayor Katie Wilson reactivated cameras in the Stadium District and approved new ones near Garfield High and Capitol Hill, adding a privacy work group. Critics question effectiveness and data sharing.

stories.h: Influencer retracts EBT fraud claim against Lam's Seafood
stories.s: Nick Shirley issued a correction saying he found no evidence the Chinatown-International District market committed fraud, and pulled his viral videos. The store says it lost customers and is weighing legal action.

stories.h: Bellevue man sues Kalshi over $308K in sports-bet losses
stories.s: Scott Bright seeks about $580,000 under Washington's gambling-loss law in federal court; Kalshi argues its federal registration makes its contracts legal and wants the case dismissed.

stories.h: King County weighs raising a Snoqualmie Valley road above floods
stories.s: The county wants feedback through Nov. 20 on elevating either Tolt Hill Road or NE 124th Street to keep SR 203 communities reachable during winter flooding.

coming.h: Westbound SR 520 closed Montlake to I-5 all weekend
coming.s: Full closure from 10 p.m. Friday to 5 a.m. Monday for expansion joint repairs; eastbound lanes and the floating bridge stay open.

coming.h: 2 Line trains replaced by buses across Lake Washington
coming.s: Saturday and Sunday, shuttles run about every 10 minutes between South Bellevue and International District/Chinatown for tunnel power work.

coming.h: Garth Brooks plays Climate Pledge Arena
coming.s: The country star brings his arena tour to Seattle Friday and Saturday.
